title: Confident and Helpful Tone
description: Copy must sound knowledgeable, direct, and supportive. Avoid defensive, timid, or apologetic phrasing.
good_example: Our platform resolves deployment rollbacks in seconds so your team stays focused on shipping features.
bad_example: We hopefully think our software might help you avoid some deployment errors if you try it.
source_quote: Speak with earned confidence: direct, clear, and reassuring without passive qualifiers.

title: Avoid Excessive Sales Hyperbole
description: Never use over-inflated hype words such as 'revolutionary', 'game-changing', 'mind-blowing', or 'miracle'. Let proven capabilities speak for themselves.
good_example: A modern event-driven telemetry pipeline designed for high-throughput workloads.
bad_example: A revolutionary, mind-blowing miracle for serverless architectures.
source_quote: Reject tech hype clichés. Describe capabilities concretely rather than resorting to hollow superlatives.

title: Respectful Competitive Stance
description: Do not insult or belittle named competitors. Focus strictly on objective technical specifications and verified architectural strengths.
good_example: Unlike legacy monoliths that poll periodically, ApexCloud streams state changes via bidirectional gRPC.
bad_example: Competitor X is clunky, ancient garbage that only clueless legacy teams still buy.
source_quote: Never disparage competitors directly; compare architectural approaches and validated performance benchmarks.

title: Customer Centricity
description: Refer to individuals and organizations using our platform as 'customers' or 'teams', never 'users', 'clients', or 'consumers'.
good_example: We partner closely with our enterprise customers across every deployment stage.
bad_example: We bill each end-user and corporate client at month end.
source_quote: Our customers are partners building serious systems; address them as 'customers' or 'engineers', never impersonal 'users'.

title: Prohibited Absolute Guarantees
description: Promotional copy must not promise unconditional guarantees or 100% outcomes without an executed Enterprise Service Level Agreement (SLA).
good_example: Architected to provide up to 99.99% availability backed by our enterprise SLA.
bad_example: We guarantee 100% uptime with zero risk and zero downtime ever.
source_quote: Avoid absolute guarantees in marketing copy. Specify engineering design parameters and SLA references.

title: Proper Product Capitalization
description: Always write 'ApexCloud' in CamelCase with no space. Writing 'Apex Cloud', 'apexcloud', or 'APEXCLOUD' is non-compliant.
good_example: The ApexCloud control plane orchestrates multi-region state replication.
bad_example: Install Apex Cloud today to monitor your clusters.
source_quote: Brand naming is fixed: 'ApexCloud' as one CamelCase word. Never split with a space.

title: Unsubstantiated Ranking Claims
description: Any claim positioning ApexCloud as 'the #1', 'the fastest', 'the best', or 'market leader' must cite an approved independent research fact or award.
good_example: Named a Leader in the 2025 Enterprise Cloud Observability Benchmark (Fact F-09).
bad_example: ApexCloud is the fastest and most popular database in the world.
source_quote: Every superlative or ranking must be accompanied by an approved industry benchmark reference.

title: Verified Performance Numbers
description: All numerical claims regarding throughput, latency, savings, and time reduction must match an active entry in the Approved Facts Vault.
good_example: Reduces end-of-month reporting latency by up to 45% based on enterprise audit data (Fact F-07).
bad_example: Cuts reporting time by 80% with instantaneous database syncing.
source_quote: Performance metrics are legal commitments. Do not cite numbers that lack active Facts Vault sign-off.

title: Mandatory Promotional Email Disclaimer
description: All outbound promotional marketing emails must include standard unsubscribing options and the legal company disclosure snippet.
good_example: You are receiving this update as an ApexCloud subscriber. Unsubscribe anytime: apexcloud.io/opt-out.
bad_example: Don't miss out on our limited time trial! Click here to activate immediately.
source_quote: Every promotional email campaign must conclude with the approved corporate entity disclosure and opt-out link.

title: Clear Call to Action (CTA)
description: Every promotional asset must conclude with a specific, direct next step rather than ambiguous invitations.
bad_example: Maybe check out our stuff if you feel like it.
source_quote: Provide action-oriented CTAs specifying the outcome: 'Start Sandbox', 'Read Architecture Whitepaper'.

title: Approved Palette Compliance
description: Visual promotional assets and social cards must draw dominant tones exclusively from the official ApexCloud color system.
good_example: Background in Deep Navy (#0F172A) with Accent Electric Blue (#2563EB) interactive accents.
bad_example: Neon green (#39FF14) background with bright magenta borders.
source_quote: Never introduce unauthorized neon or discordant novelty colors into brand visual communications.

title: Minimum Social Card Resolution
description: Images created for social promotions (LinkedIn, X) must have a minimum resolution of 1200x630 pixels to prevent pixelation.
good_example: PNG banner at 2400x1260 @ 72dpi for retina display sharpness.
bad_example: Low-resolution JPEG banner at 400x210 stretched across full width.
source_quote: Export all social preview assets at 1200x630px minimum. Never publish blurry or compressed graphics.

title: WCAG 2.1 AA Color Contrast
description: Text in visual banners and marketing copy must maintain a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 against its background (3:1 for text larger than 18pt).
good_example: White text (#FFFFFF) over Deep Navy (#0F172A) yielding a contrast ratio of 14.8:1.
bad_example: Light grey text (#9CA3AF) over White background (#FFFFFF) with a contrast ratio of 2.1:1.
source_quote: Accessibility is mandatory across all digital touchpoints. Maintain WCAG 2.1 AA compliance.

title: Mandatory Image Alt Text
description: All embedded graphics and promotional imagery must be accompanied by descriptive alternative text for screen readers.
good_example: alt='Diagram showing real-time telemetry ingestion from multi-region Kubernetes clusters into ApexCloud core'
source_quote: Images convey vital context. Provide concise, descriptive alternative text on all digital media.

title: Descriptive Link Text
description: Hyperlinks must describe the specific destination or resource. Vague phrases like 'click here', 'more', 'link', or 'read more' are prohibited.
bad_example: To see the new statistics, click here.
source_quote: Screen reader users navigate by link lists. Ensure all link text functions as an independent, meaningful label.

title: Readability Level Cap
description: General marketing and product communications should not exceed Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 10 (target grade 8) to ensure global readability.
good_example: ApexCloud tracks your server health and alerts your team when memory usage spikes.
bad_example: The epistemological underpinnings of our asynchronous distributed paradigm necessitate non-deterministic transactional synchronization.
source_quote: Write clearly for an international technical audience. Aim for Grade 8-10 readability.
